entities.summary:
Antoninus of Florence was a prominent Italian Dominican friar who served as Archbishop of Florence from 1456 to 1459. Born in the 15th century, he rose to prominence through his piety and scholarly pursuits, eventually becoming a key figure in the Catholic Church. As Archbishop, he played a crucial role in the governance of Florence and its surrounding territories.

 Antoninus of Florence was a prolific writer and translator, and his works include commentaries on the Bible and the writings of St. Augustine. He was also a skilled diplomat, serving as an emissary to the Holy See and negotiating with neighboring city-states.

 After his death in 1459, Antoninus of Florence was canonized as a saint by the Catholic Church, and his feast day is celebrated on May 11. His legacy continues to be felt in the city of Florence, where he is remembered as a devout and learned leader.

 The impact of Antoninus of Florence's life and work can be seen in the many institutions and buildings he helped establish, including the Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore and the Dominican monastery of Santa Maria delle Carceri.

 His writings, particularly his commentaries on the Bible, had a significant influence on the development of theological thought in the Renaissance.

 The legacy of Antoninus of Florence is also reflected in the many artistic and cultural works that he commissioned or patronized, including the famous painting of the 'Annunciation' by the artist Fra Angelico.
